about: Protections Rig can turn off for a while and then turns back on by itself. A step names a row by `id` and a time from `revertAfter` (minutes, `default` when left out); nothing else about it comes from outside Rig. The helper owns how each `kind` is read, turned off and turned back on (Protections.cs): `firewall` is one profile of Windows Firewall, through Windows' own firewall interface; `defender` is Microsoft Defender's real-time protection, through Defender's own settings interface, refused while Tamper Protection is on because Windows would ignore it; `registry` is one text value under HKLM that is `on` or `off`, turned off only when it reads `on` or isn't there, and turned back on by writing `on`.

`name` finishes the sentence "Turns off ...". `says` is what being without it means, for the card. Rig's background service turns a row back on when its time is up (Reverts.cs) and never does anything else with it.
User Account Control is not here: Rig's own approvals rely on it, so it is on the never list in commands.json.

rows.name: Windows Firewall on private networks
rows.says: While it's off, other devices on your home or work network can reach every program on this PC that listens for connections.

rows.name: Windows Firewall on public networks
rows.says: While it's off, anyone on the same public network, like a cafe's Wi-Fi, can reach every program on this PC that listens for connections.

rows.name: Windows Firewall on domain networks
rows.says: While it's off, other devices on your organization's network can reach every program on this PC that listens for connections.

rows.name: Microsoft Defender's real-time protection
rows.says: While it's off, Defender doesn't check files as they are opened, downloaded or run. Windows may turn it back on by itself sooner.

rows.name: SmartScreen's check of apps and files
rows.says: While it's off, Windows doesn't warn before it runs an app or file it doesn't recognize from the internet.
